director.question: q1
director.why: q1 has the highest bits at 0.112 and its confident No tests continued SN Ia fading so a Yes would refute the leader.

question.text: Brighter in r three days from now than at its last r detection?

risky.text: Brighter than 100 microjansky in g 3 days from now?

payload.rule: Every ZTF g or r measurement taken after this bet was sealed, up to one day past its last forecast, is scored against the forecast, interpolated linearly between days. The question is settled by the first r measurement within a day of its time; a limit above the reference leaves it void.

instrument.why: Persistent multi-night g- and r-band detections brighten coherently by ~1.4 mag over ~13 days after deep prior limits and fit SN Ia with chi2~0.42, not a single-night spike or erratic scatter.

implausible.why: Fitted peak at -23.3d would require ~1.4 mag brightening from ~20 to ~18.6 over ~13d to the observed peak near -7.5, whereas normal SNe II decline or plateau after peak and do not rebrighten by >1 mag

Fitted peak at -27.9d would require ~1.4 mag post-peak rebrightening to the observed peak near -7.5 and the observed blue colour g-r ~-0.1 to -0.3 is too blue for a stripped-envelope SN which is red a

theories.argument: The light curve rises from g~20 at day -20 to g~18.6/r~18.8 near day -7.5 and then fades to g~19.05 by day -0.8, matching a normal SN Ia rise-peak-decline at z=0.0703 with standard parameters x1=0.29 and c=-0.03. The SALT fit has chi2 per point of 0.42 with weight 0.86 at high Galactic latitude, consistent with an extragalactic thermonuclear transient.

refuted_if.why: A normal Ia ~10 days past maximum must keep fading in g to well below peak, so remaining at peak brightness would violate the Ia decline.

theories.weakest_point: Only a single post-peak epoch in g anchors the decline with no i-band detections to test color evolution and no sampling of the peak itself.

theories.argument: The light curve shows a smooth ~13-day rise from g~20 to a blue peak near g~18.6 with g-r ~ -0.1 to -0.3 and no prior variability over ~40 days at b=-55 deg, matching a thermal nuclear transient. The TDE fit reproduces this evolution with chi2/point 0.32 and T~10900 K, consistent with fallback-heated continuum emission.

refuted_if.why: A TDE should remain on a slow t^-5/3 blue plateau near 70-90 uJy, so this faint level would imply fading far too rapid for fallback accretion.

theories.weakest_point: Its posterior weight is only 0.042 versus 0.858 for SN Ia, and with no host image there is no evidence the source is nuclear.

theories.argument: The slow 12-day rise from g about 20 to 18.6 followed by flat r near 18.8 over 8 days matches shock cooling into a hydrogen recombination plateau at z 0.024 with absolute magnitude near minus 16.7. The blue g minus r color near zero and deep pre-explosion limits are consistent with a young hydrogen-rich explosion emerging from quiescence.

refuted_if.why: A type II should still be on its weeks-long recombination plateau near 100 uJy at this phase so a collapse that faint rules out sustained hydrogen recombination.

theories.weakest_point: The fit has chi2 per point near two with zero weight and the half-magnitude g-band fade in seven days is faster than a classic plateau.

wording.text: It is very unlikely that the distant light will be brighter than the limit in green light three days from now.
